summary: Feed s114_double to IDS is degraded: 79.5% encrypted traffic exceeds IDS 60% tolerance and 2.4% TCP packet drops indicate incomplete streams. IDS cannot inspect most payloads and misses TCP segments, reducing detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: 79.5% of bytes are encrypted (TLS), exceeding the IDS tolerance of 60%. Traffic is sent to the IDS without prior decryption - packet broker has no decrypt/forward-cleartext policy for this feed.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload for signature and anomaly detection but is blind to encrypted payloads; ~79% of traffic cannot be inspected, causing missed malware, exploit and C2 detection inside TLS.

recommended_fix.why: Decrypting at the packet broker (or forwarding a decrypted copy from TLS intercept) restores payload visibility and brings encrypted share below the IDS 60% threshold without violating its need for full payload.

findings.root_cause: 2.4% of TCP packets (60 of 2501) show gaps indicating missing data en route to tool. Tool overload is healthy and no duplicates, so drops likely from SPAN/broker buffer exhaustion or burst oversubscription feeding the 1 Gbps IDS port.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS TCP reassembly is incomplete; truncated streams cause missed signatures, broken flow reconstruction and potential evasion, leading to false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Load-balancing flows across multiple IDS instances/egress ports reduces per-port burst load and buffer drops, ensuring complete TCP streams arrive without exceeding the 1 Gbps tool capacity; also review SPAN vs TAP and broker drop counters.
